title: Local dimension-filtered flattening for a complete affine devissage
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use chartwise local finite type and local finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, with quasi-compact diagonal. A module of finite type is locally finitely generated on etale scheme charts; a finitely presented module has locally an exact presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to M\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Let $R\to A$ be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $M$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent module on $X$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be prime and put $N=\Gamma(X,M)$. Assume that $N/A/R$ admits a complete algebra devissage over $\mathfrak p$ [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage]. For a scheme $B\to Y$, write $X_B=X\times_YB$ and $M_B$ for tensor pullback. For an integer $n\geq0$, let $P_n(X,M;B)$ mean that for every representable etale scheme chart $a:U\to X_B$ and $u\in U$ mapping to $v\in B$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(u)\geq n$, the stalk $(a^*M_B)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,v}$. Residue fields, transcendence degree and base-flatness are [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Fix $d\geq0$ and assume $P_{d+1}(X,M;Y)$. There exists an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq Y$ of $\mathfrak p$ and a scheme $Z\to V$ which is a monomorphism of finite presentation, representing the functor on $V$-schemes $B$ with value $\{*\}$ if $P_d(X,M;B)$ and $\varnothing$ otherwise. Here monomorphism means that for every scheme $H$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}(H,Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,V)$ is injective; finite presentation is local finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compactness and quasi-compactness of the diagonal. No purity assumption on $M$ and no properness assumption on $X\to Y$ is made.

source.place: Tag 05UF (lemma-flat-dimension-n-representable), with complete devissage in Tags 05HH and 05HX; chart formulation from spaces-flat.tex Tag 0CWS.

proof.text: Use the Zariski--etale quasi-coherent equivalence to regard $M$ as a Zariski module. The exact-finiteness comparison preserves finite presentation, and restriction to Zariski opens has the same sections, so $N=\Gamma(X,M)$ is finitely presented by the affine-sections lemma. Let $l$ be the length of a chosen algebra devissage. We prove the stated local representability simultaneously for every affine finitely presented pair and every $d$, by induction on $l$. For $l=0$ the definition gives $N=0$, hence $M=0$: the tilde--Gamma counit identifies them. All flatness conditions then hold and the identity of $Y$ represents the functor. For $l>0$, apply the devissage preparation and replace $R$ by $R_f$ as supplied there. Every term and successive cokernel is finitely presented; write $a=a_1$ for the first smooth term's constant fibre dimension. The same preparation gives geometric integrality, base-flatness, and the universal transcendence-degree bound $a$.

source.place: 05UF, preliminary paragraph and induction setup; algebraic version 05HX and finite presentation 05HY.

proof.text: Set $Z_1=\operatorname{Spec}A_1$, $Y_1=\operatorname{Spec}B_1$, $G=\widetilde{M_1}$ on $Z_1$, and $E=\widetilde{M_1}$ on $Y_1$ with its restricted $B_1$-action. The defining module isomorphism $N\simeq M_1$ gives $M\simeq i_*G$ for the closed immersion $i:Z_1\to X$; the finite map $\pi:Z_1\to Y_1$ gives $E\simeq\pi_*G$. These are the affine tilde--Gamma identifications (sections are the same module with the indicated scalars). Apply the finite direct-image comparison twice, first to $i$ and then to $\pi$. For every scheme $T\to Y$ and every $b\geq0$ this gives $P_b(X,M;T)\iff P_b(Y_1,E;T)$, with the same all-chart criterion. In particular $E$ satisfies $P_{d+1}$ over $Y$. The preparation supplies finite presentation of $E$.

source.place: 05UF, paragraph comparing closed and finite direct image.

proof.text: If $a<d$, the universal fibre transcendence-degree bound on $Y_1$ says that no point in any base change has degree at least $d$. Thus $P_d(Y_1,E;T)$ holds for every $T$, and step 2 identifies the required functor with $h_Y$. Its representing map is the identity, a monomorphism of finite presentation.

source.place: 05UF, case d_1<d; uses the smooth ambient dimension, not equality with the support dimension.

proof.text: If $a=d$, the top-dimensional decomposition gives $F_d(Y_1,E)=\coprod_{r=0}^c H_r$ as sheaves. Represent $H_r$ by the finite-presentation locally closed immersion $S_r\to Y$ and put $Z=\coprod_{r=0}^c S_r$. A map $T\to Z$ is an open-and-closed decomposition of $T$ and a map from each piece to $S_r$, so this scheme represents precisely that sheaf coproduct. The rank decomposition is unique and each $S_r\to Y$ is a monomorphism; hence $Z\to Y$ is a monomorphism. It is of finite presentation: it is locally so on its finitely many summands, the inverse image of each affine base open is the finite union of quasi-compact inverse images in the $S_r$, and its diagonal is an isomorphism by monomorphy. Step 2 identifies its functor with the original one.

Suppose $a>d$. The generic point $\xi$ of $(Y_1)_{\mathfrak p}$ has transcendence degree $a\geq d+1$, so $P_{d+1}$ makes $E_\xi$ flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. The chosen map $\alpha_1:B_1^{\oplus r_1}\to M_1$ is an isomorphism over $\kappa(\mathfrak pB_1)$ by the devissage data. Apply generic-basis universal injectivity, with $B=B_1$ and $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pB_1$, and shrink by its $f\notin\mathfrak p$. All its hypotheses hold: the preparation gives the flat finitely presented algebra with geometrically integral fibres and the finitely presented module, while flatness at the one generic point was just checked. Put $Q=\operatorname{coker}\alpha_1$. For every base scheme $T$, the sequence $0\to\mathcal O_{(Y_1)_T}^{\oplus r_1}\to E_T\to\widetilde Q_T\to0$ is exact and remains exact after tensoring with any module over the base. Indeed this holds on affine base opens by the defining universal injectivity and tensor right exactness, and localizes to every stalk.

source.place: 05UF, case d_1>d, application of 05IA and universally exact sequence.

proof.text: At a point $x\in(Y_1)_T$ over $t\in T$, write $K=\mathcal O_{T,t}$ and $U\to V\to W$ for the stalk sequence of step 5. Here $U$ is $K$-flat because $(Y_1)_T\to T$ is smooth and flat, and the sequence is universally exact over $K$. If $V$ is flat then the flat-cokernel lemma makes $W$ flat. Conversely let $W$ be flat. For an injection $L\to L'$ and $z\in L\otimes_K V$ killed in $L'\otimes_K V$, its image in $L\otimes_K W$ is zero by flatness of $W$. Lift $z$ from $u\in L\otimes_K U$ by tensor right exactness. Universal injectivity in the $L'$ row and flatness of $U$ force $u=0$, so $z=0$. Thus tensoring $V$ preserves injections, which is flatness. Consequently $E_T$ and $\widetilde Q_T$ have exactly the same flatness locus, and their $P_b$ conditions agree for all $b$.

source.place: 05UF, equality of flatness loci after universally injective free subtraction; direct tensor diagram chase for the reverse implication.

proof.text: The tail $(A_i,B_i,M_i,\alpha_i)_{i=2}^l$ is a complete algebra devissage of $Q/B_1/R$ over $\mathfrak p$, directly by the cokernel identifications in the definition. For $l=1$ it is the permitted empty devissage, since $Q=0$. The preparation gives that $B_1$ is finitely presented over $R$ and $Q$ finitely presented over $B_1$; step 6 gives $P_{d+1}(Y_1,\widetilde Q;Y)$. The induction hypothesis, now at the strictly smaller length $l-1$, therefore represents $P_d(Y_1,\widetilde Q;-)$ over a further open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$ by a finite-presentation monomorphism. Steps 2 and 6 identify this with the original functor on every base test. All comparisons are compatible with restriction, since they identify singleton-or-empty subfunctors of $h_Y$. The sheaf property and one-atlas criterion ensure the affine constructions and comparisons apply on arbitrary base schemes: cover a test by affine opens, use the same comparisons there, and glue the unique morphisms into the representing scheme. This completes the induction; no ordering of the $a_i$, purity, or properness was used.

source.place: 05UF, induction on the cokernel tail and the preliminary affine-test reduction; 05HX, rather than an unjustified identification with 05HH.

proof_origin.place: 05UF proof, adapted explicitly from geometric devissage to the weaker 05HX algebraic data; 05HY, 05IA, 05UE and 05UC are the supporting inputs.
